text:
Alex Kim: Kicked off a focused smoke run to compare seqlen distribution impacts + KV cache thrash across 4 GPU/driver combos. Using replay harness vs synthetic. Observed ~2x variance in p95 for same QPS. posting quick notes.

Priya Nair: TL;DR — noise concentrated when seqlen > 512 and when KV hit rate drops below ~70%.

Ryan Ortega: What machines + drivers? image tags?

Alex Kim: gpus: A100-80GB (driver 525.85), H100 (driver 535.86), V100 (470.57), A10G (525.85). containers: ci-runtime:v2026-03-15 (sha256:abcd1234), ci-runtime:v2026-03-16 (sha256:efgh5678). kernel flags: they vary — some runs used `TF32_FORCE_ENABLE=0`, others default. replay harness used trace id `replay-2026-03-01-001`. synthetic traffic generated from seqlen-mixer (short/long ratio 70/30).

Jamie Liu: profiler snapshots or kernel_selector logs you can share?

Alex Kim: small sample from the run:

```
[2026-03-15 12:02:45] kernel_selector: chosen=matmul_fused_v2 reason=low_seq_len score=0.82
[2026-03-15 12:02:46] batching: window_ms=10 batch_target=32 effective_batch=28
[2026-03-15 12:02:47] kv_cache: hit_rate=0.68 eviction_count=123
[2026-03-15 12:02:48] kernel_selector: chosen=matmul_split_v1 reason=high_seq_len score=0.90
```

Priya Nair: that flip in kernel_selector around long seqlens matches the p95 cliff. If matmul_fused_v2 has poor long-seqlen scaling it explains the regression.

Ryan Ortega: also noticed continuous batching heuristics will shrink the window when variance spikes, which increases syscall overhead and kills throughput. We saw effective_batch bounce between 8 and 32 under thrash.

Marta Chen: infra-bot: nightly-loadtest finished, artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-loadtests/2098765432/ with metadata.json (includes driver, kernel-cmdline, docker digests).

Alex Kim: action items: (1) pin driver+image combinations for apples-to-apples (we need deterministic baselines), (2) add seqlen-aware KV warmup in the replay harness to avoid cold-hit storms, (3) add an override in kernel_selector to prefer stable variant for seqlen > 1024 and re-run smoke. I'll open PRs for (1)+(2) today.

Jamie Liu: +1. Also please include kernel boot flags and `nvidia-smi --query` output in artifact metadata — makes triage faster.

Ryan Ortega: I'll take batching microbench: run deterministic microbench with fixed window and static seqlens to see if heuristic is mis-tuned. Will post numbers.

Priya Nair: suggestion: add a small spike test in synthetic suite that inserts a long-seqlen burst every 30s to simulate user patterns that thrash KV. That caught the issue locally for me.

Alex Kim: good idea. tagging @Jamie Liu @Ryan Ortega for a quick sync tomorrow 09:30 PT. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
